feed.title: Combined summary - We made the bitcoin-dev mailing list readable: 15 years, 24,699 messages

entry.title: Combined summary - We made the bitcoin-dev mailing list readable: 15 years, 24,699 messages
entry.summary: A new, user-friendly mirror of the bitcoin-dev mailing list archive has been established, offering daily updates to ensure that its content remains current. This archive departs from previous solutions by providing a more organized structure: each discussion thread is presented on an individual page, with quoted text efficiently folded to enhance readability. Messages are accessible through stable permalinks based on Message-ID, ensuring consistency and ease of citation. Three comprehensive indexes have been implemented, allowing users to navigate topics chronologically, explore every BIP (Bitcoin Improvement Proposal) discussed, and view contributions from each author on dedicated pages. All original messages are preserved without alteration, with the only editorial intervention being succinct topic summaries designed to help orient readers. Each message includes a direct link to its source location, promoting transparency and verifiability. The archive’s management of author identities involves merging various spellings or forms associated with a single email address into unified author pages—such as combining names like “Luke-Jr” and “Luke Dashjr”—while intentionally keeping distinct mailing list or group addresses separate. Users can request corrections or express preferences regarding these author attributions at any time. Thread association is primarily determined through reference headers; when these are missing, subject line matching within a 180-day period is used to reconstruct discussion threads. Any inaccuracies in thread organization can be swiftly addressed upon notification. The resource also seeks community feedback regarding its inclusion among the official [public archives of the list](https://www.openai.com), while remaining considerate of requests for exclusion. The primary aim is to enhance access and usability for participants and followers of bitcoin-dev discussions, with ongoing improvements guided by user input. Efficient chronological browsing is a cornerstone of the archive’s design. A prominent navigation section titled “Years” offers a comprehensive listing of all years since 2011, accompanied by the number of threads initiated each year. Within each year’s page, threads are grouped by month and ordered according to the date of their first message, providing a clear view of the development timeline throughout the year. Month headings serve as anchors, enabling instant navigation to specific months, and a row of month links at the top of each year page further streamlines this process. The homepage features a “Recently active” list, which presents the most recent messages in descending order, facilitating rapid access to the latest developments. To improve clarity and user experience, the main navigation entry was renamed from “Numbers” to “Years,” and enhanced with a new month bar, following feedback from users. The archive has expanded to include detailed information about the integration of BIPs into Bitcoin Core. Every BIP page now features an “In Bitcoin Core” box, displaying the version in which the BIP was first included, subsequent versions that affected it, and verbatim notes from Core’s doc/bips.md, including relevant pull request links. For example, [BIP 141’s page](https://www.learnbitcoin.com/archive/bips/141) lists all related threads alongside versioning milestones such as “0.13.0, defined for mainnet as of 0.13.1, buried since 0.19.0.” This feature covers all 74 BIPs referenced in doc/bips.md. Additionally, there are individual pages for each of the 137 Bitcoin Core releases, starting from version 0.1.5, available at [the archive’s release index](https://www.learnbitcoin.com/archive/releases). These pages provide release dates, associated discussion threads, the BIPs first shipped in each release, and links to release notes. The mapping between BIPs and releases is tied to the accuracy of doc/bips.md; users are encouraged to report discrepancies or omissions so corrections can be made upstream and reflected in the next refresh. As part of continued improvements, the archive now updates twice daily, and duplicate author pages caused by split email addresses have been consolidated. This structured approach to archiving and navigation significantly enhances the accessibility and utility of the bitcoin-dev mailing list for developers, researchers, and community members, supporting both historical exploration and tracking of ongoing development.
